title: [finding] Four self-contained `packages/spec/src` TSDoc examples do not compile — the root `index.ts` teaches an `@objectstack/spec/auth` subpath that does not exist
body:
Found by the sweep #10924's triage put in scope ("the suggested co-check is in-scope as a sweep, **findings filed not folded**"). Filed, not folded: repairing these is not #10924's scope — that card builds the gate. PR #11433 adds the surface and marks the six blocks that compile; these four are left unmarked and unrepaired.

## How they were found

With the new `packages/spec/src` surface active, every one of the 146 fenced ts blocks in that tree was extracted. 128 carry no import of their own and three more are ellipsis-placeholder prose, so 15 self-contained blocks were type-checked against the built `@objectstack/spec` declarations, the same way the gate does (`paths` map derived from the package's own `exports`).

Note the first run proved nothing and was discarded — the three ellipsis fragments' TS1109 syntax errors suppress `tsc`'s semantic pass for the whole program, exactly the trap `check-skill-examples.ts`'s header documents. The diagnostics below come from the re-run with those excluded.

## The four

### 1. `packages/spec/src/index.ts` — three blocks, the package's front door

The file's own header documents three import styles. All three name things that do not exist:

```
index.ts:15  TS2305: Module '"@objectstack/spec"' has no exported member 'Data'.
index.ts:15  TS2305: Module '"@objectstack/spec"' has no exported member 'UI'.
index.ts:15  TS2305: Module '"@objectstack/spec"' has no exported member 'System'.
index.ts:15  TS2305: Module '"@objectstack/spec"' has no exported member 'Auth'.
index.ts:15  TS2305: Module '"@objectstack/spec"' has no exported member 'AI'.
index.ts:15  TS2305: Module '"@objectstack/spec"' has no exported member 'API'.
index.ts:26  TS2307: Cannot find module '@objectstack/spec/auth' or its corresponding type declarations.
index.ts:35  TS2307: Cannot find module '@objectstack/spec/auth' or its corresponding type declarations.
```

Two distinct defects here:

- **`@objectstack/spec/auth` is not an exported subpath.** The package's `exports` declares `./identity` (User, Organization, Profile), not `./auth`. Styles 2 and 3 both instruct the reader to import `Auth.User` / `{ User, Session }` from a specifier that cannot resolve.
- **Style 1's root namespace imports do not exist either** — which the prose two lines above arguably already concedes ("This package does NOT export types at the root level"), making the block and its own preamble disagree.

This is the highest-value instance in the sweep: it is the first docblock in the package's entry point, i.e. the first thing an AI author reads.

### 2. `packages/spec/src/shared/branded-types.zod.ts:14`

```
branded-types.zod.ts:15  TS2305: Module '"@objectstack/spec"' has no exported member 'ObjectNameSchema'.
branded-types.zod.ts:15  TS2305: Module '"@objectstack/spec"' has no exported member 'FieldNameSchema'.
```

Both symbols exist — `export const ObjectNameSchema` / `FieldNameSchema` are declared in this very file and re-exported through `shared/index.ts`. The example simply names the wrong specifier: they resolve from `@objectstack/spec/shared`, not the root.

## Suggested repair

Rewrite each block against the current `exports` map and built declarations, then **add the `<!-- os:check -->` marker** so the gate keeps them honest — that marker is what makes the repair permanent rather than a point fix. Acceptance is mechanical: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:skill-examples` stays green with four more marked blocks (10 on the spec-source surface instead of 6).

Worth deciding during the work, and the reason this is filed rather than guessed: whether the root `index.ts` header should document the namespace-import style at all, or be rewritten around the subpath styles that do resolve. That is a docs-shape question about the package's front door, not a mechanical rename, and it is why these were not folded into #11433.

Splittable if preferred — `index.ts` and `branded-types.zod.ts` share a defect class and an acceptance test but no code.
